verdict.tagline: A masterpiece of tension, provided you survive the technical hurdles.
not_for_you_if: you need stable performance on modern pc displays
you dislike repetitive backtracking and scarce resources

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players within the refund window report technical issues with modern displays alongside demanding save systems and opaque mechanics.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as broken on modern PCs, noting issues with high refresh rates causing bullet mode with vsync, problems with slow mouse movements, and poorly functioning brightness adjustment on OLED screens.

citations.review_text:
Game is broken on modern PCs. 240 hz is not possible with vsync. It will turn the game into bullet mode. Mouse has issues with very slow movements. 
Brightness adjustment on an OLED screen is a joke. 

Can't believe they haven't adressed any of these uses for the past years.

Unplayable on mouse. If you move your mouse below a certain speed threshold it does this very low static sensitivity. So unless you're flicking for every little movement, you're going to feel a stutter every time you move your mouse. I tried every sensitivity, dpi, framrate cap, v sync, g sync, and other settings in nvidia control panel and it was always there.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that nothing is explained to the player regarding game systems, requiring outside guides to play without frustration.

citations.review_text: If your a fan of alien isolation than sure its a great game but besides for that its really poorly play tested the ai feels stupid and nothing is shown or explained to the player so the only way to play the game without slaming ur head against a wall is through guides which is really lame

I've had this game for a while now. I played it when I first bought it, but put it down after about an hour because I struggled with the pacing. I recently decided to revisit it, and after giving it more time, I had a much better experience overall, though not without some frustrations.

I still haven’t completed it, but I’m steadily working my way through. The Alien mechanic is very different and genuinely interesting, adding a lot of tension to the gameplay. However, the fixed save points can be frustrating, at one point I got caught around 10 times, with the nearest save being about 20 minutes earlier, which really started to test my patience.

The weapons and crafted items also felt less useful than I expected. Most of the time I avoided using them because they often just attracted the Alien to my location, although they did come in handy a few times for dealing with aggressive human enemies.

So far, it’s mostly been a good experience, you just need patience, especially when the Alien keeps finding you and resetting your progress.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players praise the smooth optimization and scarcity that drives stealth, while noting repetitive tasks and frustrating combat sections.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs with high frame rates and strong optimization on modern PC hardware.

citations.review_text:
Alien: Isolation 2 is doomed to fail.
There is no way the devs will be able to match this game's level of quality and performance,
especially using UE5-slop engine.
Unless they watch Threat Interactive's tutorial on how to optimize games or something...

Anyway, this game is amazing. On all levels and aspects.

Q: Would I recommend?
A: Absolutely!

[+]
1) Great performance/optimization
No stutters, no upscaling or frame generation bullpoop,
the game just runs 200+ FPS on native 4K without any problem on a high-end PC.
2) Faithful replication of the original style
3) Phenomenal lighting
4) Immersive atmosphere
5) Terrifying sounds/ambience
6) Engaging/immersive in-game interaction
7) Tension-making animations
8) Amazing design and style
9) Good story and characters
10) Clean UI and controls
11) Immersive gameplay
12) A lot of craftable gadgets that are actually useful

[-]
1) No in-game FPS limiter
2) Some minor texture flickering
3) No main character shadow
4) Early flamethrower
The flamethrower is used too early in the game,
making all other craftable gadgets almost useless...
5) Some occasional sound bugs
I have a suspicion it's only limited to playing the game on Linux.

Conclusion: 10/10

Alien Isolation is a true survival horror master piece that is done right. Through out the game you are provided with weapons to help you fight back. However, since finding resources like ammo is very difficult in game, engaging in combat is highly discouraged which makes Alien Isolation an amazing game as it focusses on the horror aspect rather then combat. The main stalker which is the Xenomorph (alien) also has the best AI out of any horror game because you constantly have to change tactics every time you encounter it. This game also has amazing optimization for modern hardware. I highly recommend this game if you are interested in survival horror.
Absolutely incredible game. This is my second time playing through the game, but on pc. The game runs extremely well, and still looks great. Would absolutely recommend to anyone!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the PC port can display compatibility warnings on boot when using certain graphics cards, leading to visual glitches such as floating weapons.

citations.review_text:
Pretty good but this port is not exactly the smoothest. As soon as you boot it will likely tell you you're drivers not compatible (guaranteed not compatible if you're on AMD or Intel gpu). This doesnt mean you cant play but means theres a good chance of bugs/glitches happening. The glitch i see most frequently is enemy weapons levitating in the air, which actually made it so that they cant shoot you cause theyre now unarmed (humans are the least threatening enemy so might not be as experience breaking). I've never outright game crashed though.

Aside from the rough port it's a really good game. I highly suggest playing on hard to up the survival aspects. You being vulnerable while saving make for some really tense moments. The crafting system is pretty mid, although there is a choice of using limited materials to craft one item over another, some items are clearly more useful than others (pipe bomb and molotov > everything else). The game is at its most fun when its just you and one alien stalking you, it becomes pretty frustrating when its more than one alien or an alien plus androids or humans. The alien by itself is already extremely lethal so adding more threats feels unfair. At some point you get a flamethrower to scare off the alien, some may think this trivializes alien encounters but it feels fair since there some relatively small rooms where you just need the alien off of you so you can solve the puzzle in peace (it's not gone for long though). The sound design is really good, hearing the aliens footsteps getting closer, hearing it move through the vents, hearing it sense your presence and make a short screech, really adds to the fear.

7/10, while this is a great game I ran into a series of technical problems and very odd issues with AI detection on normal that I just gave up trying to get things to work. Yes the game is good but your milage may vary in this hit or miss PC Port.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign as repetitive, citing recurring tasks like hacking, using the blowtorch, pulling levers, and backtracking.

citations.review_text:
I really wanted to love this game and I am sure that for most players who love the Alien franchise this game will be a gem. Not for me though. It was stretched thin. Becomes repetitive very quickly.
Positives: The Alien is adorable and scared the living ♥♥♥♥ out of me without failing even once.
Negatives: Repetition is the killer of my joy...

9/10 Phenominal game. The game has amazing atmosphere and sound engineering! Gameplay is pretty simple and basic but fun sometimes a little glitchy with the alien and fire type mechanics (flamethrower, molotov). I enjoyed the little hacking games. But eventually everything becomes kind of repetitive the hacking, blow torch and pulling levers. 
Enemy design is pretty good especially the alien it's super cool and how their tail moves and flops around. The cutscenes truly make the game that much better! Looking forward to Alien Isolation 2!

Like many other people, I really wanted to like this game. And while there are some good moments, they are completely eaten away by some very bad choices. Graphics are great, but design is boring; white corridors with computers and lockers, over and over again. Half of deaths felt undeserved and random. The game has only one puzzle - go to the other side of the station, play a mini game to open the door, pull the switch, get back, don't get killed by Alien in the process... Now repeat 50 more times... Some games are known to have unsatisfying endings, but this one must be number one (spoiler: it just ends, goodbye). And, worst of all, this game seriously overstays its welcome. Needless to say I haven't touched the DLC. The reason people like this game is because of Xenomorph, and we all like Xenomorph. Let's face it, if it was some other entity, game wouldn't do nearly as well as it did.

Good before bad. Gameplay spoilers below and keep in mind I played on 'hard'.

Great atmosphere. Fantastic tension. Engaging story.

The alien can and will see you without even looking at you. The alien noticing you at all is pretty much a game over, even with the weapon you use to fend it off, on hard it takes more shots by default, the alien naturally gets more resistant the more you use it, and seems to come back almost immediately so I hope you found a decent place to hide. The alien also learns where you like to hide, which I actually like... until you're forced into a dead end hallway to progress the mission with only a gurney to hide under. The androids seem to have extendable arms so I hope you love spamming your keyboard to make them let go and them tanking five point blank revolver rounds to the head when there's 2-3 chasing you isn't fun, it's annoying. I went into mission 11-12  with 30+ rounds and ended with less than 12, keep in mind I found ammo in the missions and also used the shotgun as well as other resources too. Oh and the revolver reticle lies when at mid-longish distance. I've missed too many shots on stationary androids that I did the gamer lean to ensure I hit. All of this could be countered by "git gud". I agree. What can also be unanimously agreed upon, though, is how absurdly annoying it is to die to something that was completely unpredictable and out of your control, and now you have to do 20 minutes of sneaking around again flipping levers and finding keycards. Now take that, and expand it to two separate missions (so far) taking me nearly 2 hours to do.

Overall, great game I'll likely never play once I beat it, or at the very least, never again on hard lol.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that human and android enemy sections are frustrating or poorly designed compared to encounters with the xenomorph.

citations.review_text: Its clear that while visually the game is still in decent shape today, there is some very apparent clunkiness from the early 2010s. the AI of the xenomorphs is still really good but the same cant be said for the humans, words cannot describe how stupid they are and their sections are easily the worst part of the game. There is also quite questionable encounter balancing with the alien, especially early on in the hospital but i found that challenge kinda fun to overcome. Despite all that, the game is easily one of the best in the genre to this day.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players highlight the dynamic artificial intelligence governing unpredictable encounters, alongside less terrifying sections against androids.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the artificial intelligence governing the alien causes each encounter and playthrough to feel random and different.

citations.review_text: A fav game of mine as a longtime Alien fan! Can't wait to play the sequel (hopefully soon!) Has good scare factor and pressure from the alien. My only recommendation is to play on a more difficult setting! The Ai sometimes gets stuck in a loop and traps you in a hiding spot.
How each game is completly random.
One of (if not) the best horror game ever made, very complex AI behavior that makes each encounter with the alien different.

Hands down, one of the best horror games I’ve played. I’ve played it through several times and it never gets old. The fear factor never goes away because each gameplay is different- aside from the storyline which the game follows. The alien learns from each player with its unique ai powered programming that was ahead of its time during the initial release of the game. To this day, the aliens programming still is unmatched by any game so far. Something I’ve learned, is the more unpredictable the player becomes- the more unpredictable the alien becomes as well. There’s also plenty of opportunities between objectives to explore different areas of Sevastopol. This means more loot, finding things you missed the first time through, or gaining access to parts of the map you couldn’t previously due to insufficient tools.  Awesome game, can’t wait to play the sequel.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features sections where players encounter androids instead of the alien, which some find less scary over time.

citations.review_text: This game is still tense even 12 years later. The graphics held up surprisingly well. My only critique is that there are some sections where it meanders a bit because the alien isn't around. Fighting off androids is only scary the first couple of times. After a while of that, I started wishing for the alien to come back. Which I guess is a good sign, because that alien is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrifying. The AI was so advanced for its time, and even now, the way it learns from you really adds a whole other level to the game. So A++ for that.

Negatives: Kitty doesnt like pets :(

Positives: great graphics still to this day, I dont think this game has had or needed a patch or update since it released. Its perfect.

This game is amazing. If your looking to suck in the lore, theres plenty of lore to find via voice memos and terminals. If your looking to explore then theres plenty to see. If you wanna trigger your fear of mannequins theres plenty of angry mannequin people. If you wanna play cat and mouse with the pissiest cat you ever met then here you go.
